lesson_title: Kinetic Energy: Double the Speed, Four Times the Danger
hook_text: Double your speed and the crash gets FOUR times worse. One tiny ² decides it.
clip_script: An 800 kilogram bakkie at 15 metres per second — 54 on the speedometer. Its kinetic energy: half of 800 times 15 squared — 90 000 joules. That is a 4 kilogram paint tin lifted two kilometres straight up, riding along on an ordinary trip. Now the driver doubles the speed to 30. Recount the wallet: 30 squared is 900 — 360 000 joules. Double the speed, FOUR times the energy, because the speed multiplies by itself. Four times the energy means four times the braking distance, and in a crash, four times the wreckage. A collision at 80 is four collisions at 40 happening at once. That little squared symbol is the whole science of speed limits.
visual_style: A bakkie's energy drawn as a coin stack that suddenly quadruples when the speedometer doubles; braking-distance bars stretch from 1x to 4x; the ² glows red in the formula.
mood: Sober jolt delivered with clean arithmetic.
pacing: Calm setup at 54 km/h, sharp gear-change to the doubling, hammer-blow of the four-times reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and count a moving wallet yourself.
